items.summary: CTO review: approve the containment disposition. Delivery is saturated at 10/10 active slots, so reject new production work, prototypes, site-factory admissions, telemetry changes, spend, dependencies, credentials, and duplicate queue requests. Complete or close the existing saveusfarms.com repair case with dated root-cause or closure evidence, deterministic tests, isolated validation, build evidence, rollback point, release boundary, attribution limits, measurement limits, and deduplication evidence by 2026-10-01T09:00Z. Only after one slot is released may the already-queued allthingsmasonic.com CTA refinement proceed. The CTA change is technically feasible as a bounded single-site implementation using existing assets and architecture, with deterministic tests, link/build validation, accessibility checks, preview review, and single-diff rollback. Measure only the existing affiliate-click metric boundary; do not claim revenue, ROI, or causal lift.

Do not admit the proposed site-factory pipeline this cycle. The candidate scaffold has analytics unconfigured, compliance failures, and unavailable operations/security clearance evidence; therefore public exposure and production implementation are not technically supportable. Retain any launch-readiness work as a non-delivery prerequisite using existing evidence paths only. No new telemetry, dependencies, domains, credentials, deployment, or external spend is authorized.

Keep the private launch and security-sensitive release gates unchanged. Existing operations and fleet-doctor evidence is unavailable, so no security clearance or release certification should be inferred. Preserve Amazon results as aggregate and unattributed for the recorded window; require registered site tracking IDs for future affiliate links. No additional measurement request is needed because the shared telemetry already covers the approved CTA metric boundary.
